children: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries plans to invest about $800 million in power-engine and small-reactor businesses to meet surging electricity demand from artificial-intelligence data centers.

The South Korean company said Thursday its board approved a combined 1.072 trillion won investment, equivalent to $799.9 million, to build new production facilities in South Korea for gas-powered HiMSEN engines used to generate electricity and key components for small modular reactors.
Of the total, 833.6 billion won will go toward a new power-engine plant in Ulsan. Construction is expected to start in the first quarter of 2027, with operations scheduled to begin in May 2028.

The remaining 238.6 billion won will be used to build production facilities for main SMR components within the company's existing shipyard compound in Ulsan. The company expects to complete the SMR manufacturing facilities in the first half of 2029.

HD Hyundai Heavy said the investment is aimed at strengthening its competitiveness in power engines and SMRs, which are gaining attention as new power sources in the AI era, and responding proactively to surging electricity demand.
